description: Cut the list at exactly 10 rows. Which of the tied customers make the cut is arbitrary.

b.request: Top 10 customers by order count share (customer id, number of orders, and that count divided by the total number of orders, unrounded), sorted by share from highest to lowest with nulls last, limited to exactly 10 rows, where ties at the cutoff are broken arbitrarily
b.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS num_orders, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

a.request: For each customer in the orders table, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share of all orders (their count divided by the total number of orders). Sort by share from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and return exactly 10 rows. If several customers are tied at the 10th place, pick any of them to fill the remaining spots. Don't round anything.
a.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

c.request: Which are the top 10 customers by share of all orders? For each, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share (their order count divided by the total number of orders), sorted from highest to lowest share with missing values last. Don't round anything. Cut the list at exactly 10 rows. Which of the tied customers make the cut is arbitrary.
c.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Which are the top 10 customers by share of all orders? For each, show the customer id, how many orders they placed, and their share (their order count divided by the total number of orders), sorted from highest to lowest share with missing values last. Don't round anything. Limit the result to exactly 10 rows, and if customers are tied at the cutoff, it doesn't matter which of the tied customers are included.
d.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) AS share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
